newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-FORMER CAPTAINS HOUGHTON AND FLOWER STRIKE CENTURIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FORMER CAPTAINS HOUGHTON AND FLOWER STRIKE CENTURIES.

text.p: Former Zimbabwe captains Dave Houghton and Andy Flower struck contrasting centuries on Saturday on the opening day of the tourists' three-day match against a Pakistan Cricket Board Combined XI.
Houghton, 39, hammered 17 fours and two sixes as he raced to his century off just 115 balls before he was bowled for 105 by home side captain and left-arm spinner Aamir Sohail.
Flower was altogether more circumspect, taking 166 minutes in his even unbeaten century which contained 13 fours and a six.
Skipper Alistair Campbell declared the Zimbabwe innings closed at 307 for seven after Flower reached his century and at the close the Board XI were eight without loss.

Zimbabwe slumped to 36 for three after Campbell had won the toss and elected to bat but Houghton and Flower then revived their fortunes with a 131-run partnership for the fourth wicket of which Flower contributed only 11.
Houghton was especially severe on left-arm spinner Mohammad Hussain, who conceded 28 runs from two overs.
Teenager pace bowler Shahid Nazir was the most successful bowler with three for 42 while Sohail captured two for 32.
The tourists play a two-test series and three one-day internationals.
